headline: The Senate blocked H.J.Res. 61, which would have exempted people covered by TRICARE or VA health care from the ACA employer coverage mandate.
what_it_does: If adopted, this joint resolution would change the Internal Revenue Code so that employees with coverage under a Department of Defense health program, such as TRICARE, or a Department of Veterans Affairs health program would not count as eligible employees for the Affordable Care Act employer mandate. The employer mandate requires large employers to offer minimum essential health coverage to eligible employees. The measure would also keep its budget effects off both PAYGO scorecards under the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.

who_it_affects.group: Employees covered by TRICARE or other Department of Defense health programs
who_it_affects.how: They would not be counted as eligible employees for their employer's ACA coverage requirement.

who_it_affects.group: Employees covered by Department of Veterans Affairs health care
who_it_affects.how: They would not be counted as eligible employees for their employer's ACA coverage requirement.

who_it_affects.group: Applicable large employers under the ACA
who_it_affects.how: They would not have to count employees with military or VA health coverage when deciding whether they must offer minimum essential coverage.
